extraction.method: axios call sites read out of the pinned helper with magic-regexp, one call per exported function

sessionModel.gate: pages/Home.tsx calls GET /api/user/me on mount and replaces history with /signin unless it yields a user
sessionModel.transport: axios sets withCredentials, so the real backend carries a cookie; the loopback API seam carries no headers, so the projection holds the session as per-run in-memory state instead
sessionModel.signup: the sign-up button appears only while GET /api/status reports no owner; the projection grants OWNER only when no owner exists and records a USER otherwise

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as SystemStatus: `owner` decides the sign-in button, `profile.mode` prefills the form when it is "dev"
endpoints.note: The only route the pinned client calls before a session exists. An absent owner turns the sign-in button into "Sign up as Owner".

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as User; Signin discards the body and re-reads the session through userService.doSignIn
endpoints.note: A non-2xx makes axios throw, which the page turns into a toast; the projection answers 401 for values it does not hold.

endpoints.request: { email, password, role, name } — the page always sends role "OWNER"
endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as User
endpoints.note: Reachable only while /api/status reports no owner. The projection grants OWNER only when no owner exists and otherwise records a USER.

endpoints.response: ignored — userService clears the store before it calls
endpoints.note: Sign-out is what puts the session gate back in force for the next navigation.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as User; MemberSection refetches the list afterwards
endpoints.note: Owner-only in the settings dialog; the projection answers 403 for a non-owner session.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as User; userService converts createdTs/updatedTs from seconds to milliseconds
endpoints.note: THE session gate. Home.tsx replaces history with /signin whenever this does not yield a user, so every behind-the-gate journey depends on it.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as User[] rendered by the member table
endpoints.note: Same path as createUser, disambiguated by method alone.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as User, merged into the store
endpoints.note: The account-settings surface: display name, password change and open-id reset all arrive here. Preference toggles never do — they are localStorage only.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as Memo[]; memoService drops ARCHIVED rows client-side and rescales timestamps
endpoints.note: The list the home page renders. Search, tag filter and type filter are computed client-side in helpers/filter.ts over exactly this payload.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as Memo[] rendered by the recycle-bin dialog
endpoints.note: Same route as getMemoList with a hard-coded query, so the projection has to honour rowStatus rather than always returning everything.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as Memo, prepended to the store
endpoints.note: The editor save path, and also the JSON import in PreferencesSection which supplies its own createdTs.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as Memo
endpoints.note: Carries three journeys at once: edit content, archive (rowStatus ARCHIVED) and restore from the recycle bin (rowStatus NORMAL).

endpoints.response: ignored — the store patch is applied optimistically
endpoints.note: Shares one route with unpinMemo; only the body differs.

endpoints.response: ignored — the store patch is applied optimistically
endpoints.note: The second half of the organizer route.

endpoints.response: ignored
endpoints.note: Permanent delete from the recycle bin, distinct from the archive patch above.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as Shortcut[]; the sidebar splits them by rowStatus into pinned and unpinned
endpoints.note: Fetched on ShortcutList mount, so it is part of the first behind-the-gate paint.

endpoints.request: ShortcutCreate { title, payload } where payload is a JSON-encoded filter array
endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as Shortcut
endpoints.note: The saved-search journey: the dialog encodes the active filters into payload.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as Shortcut
endpoints.note: Rename, re-filter, and pin/unpin — the sidebar pins a shortcut by setting rowStatus ARCHIVED.

endpoints.response: ignored
endpoints.note: Removes the shortcut from the sidebar list.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as Resource; the editor inserts `![](/h/r/{id}/{filename})` into the memo body
endpoints.note: WITHHELD. No journey uploads a file, and the inserted URL points at a `/h/r/:id/:filename` byte stream outside /api that the projection would also have to invent. The projection refuses it as a named withheld endpoint rather than fabricating a resource pipeline.

endpoints.response: ResponseObject<T> — the UI reads `response.data.data` as string[] rendered by the sidebar tag list
endpoints.note: Server-derived in the real backend. The projection derives it from the seeded memo content under the client's own `#tag ` rule so the tag list and the client-side tag filter agree.

clientOnlySurfaces.surface: search, tag filter and type filter
clientOnlySurfaces.implementation: src/helpers/filter.ts over the already-fetched memo list
clientOnlySurfaces.note: No request is issued when the user searches or picks a tag; the filter runs against the store.

clientOnlySurfaces.surface: editor preferences (split words, hide image urls, markdown parser)
clientOnlySurfaces.note: Preference toggles never reach the API. Only account settings (name, password, open-id reset) do, through PATCH /api/user/me.
Reachable only after an upload, which the projection withholds.

withheldEndpoints.reason: no journey uploads a file; projecting an upload would mean inventing a resource pipeline and a `/h/r/:id/:filename` byte stream that no witness observes

scope: API projection only: this unit publishes no journeys, no witness receipt and no witness run entry.
